title: Rock Quality Designation (RQD) from Core
equation: RQD = (Σ lengths of intact core ≥ 100 mm) / (total core run length) × 100%
applicability: Measured on NX (54.7 mm) or larger diameter core. Double-tube or triple-tube barrel required. Natural fractures only — exclude mechanical breaks (fresh, rough surfaces, fit together). Classification: < 25% very poor, 25–50% poor, 50–75% fair, 75–90% good, 90–100% excellent.

title: RQD from Volumetric Joint Count

Jv.description: Volumetric joint count = sum of frequencies of all joint sets

applicability: For Jv > 4.5. When Jv ≤ 4.5, RQD = 100%. Jv = Σ(1/Si) where Si = mean spacing of joint set i. Useful when no core is available — estimate from exposure mapping.

title: RQD from Mean Discontinuity Frequency

RQD.description: Estimated RQD along a given direction

λ.description: Mean discontinuity frequency (all sets) along the measurement direction

applicability: Theoretical relationship assuming negative exponential spacing distribution. λ = number of discontinuities per meter along scanline. This is directional RQD — varies with measurement direction.

title: Q-System Rock Mass Classification

RQD.description: Rock Quality Designation (10–100, use 10 as minimum)

applicability: Three quotients: RQD/Jn = block size, Jr/Ja = shear strength of critical joint, Jw/SRF = active stress. Classification: Q < 0.01 exceptionally poor, 0.01–0.1 extremely poor, 0.1–1 very poor, 1–4 poor, 4–10 fair, 10–40 good, 40–100 very good, 100–400 extremely good, > 400 exceptionally good.

title: RMR — Rock Mass Rating (Bieniawski 1989)
equation: RMR = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + R₄ + R₅ + adjustment
applicability: Total 0–100. Class I: > 80 (very good). II: 61–80 (good). III: 41–60 (fair). IV: 21–40 (poor). V: < 20 (very poor). Correlations: cohesion, friction angle, stand-up time, support requirements.

title: Point Load Strength Index

Is(50).description: Point load strength index corrected to 50 mm equivalent diameter

De.description: Equivalent core diameter: De = D for diametral test; De = √(4WD/π) for irregular

applicability: Size correction normalizes to De = 50 mm reference. UCS ≈ K × Is(50), K = 20–25 typical. For anisotropic rocks, test parallel and perpendicular to foliation. Minimum 10 tests recommended; reject lowest and highest, average remainder.

title: Schmidt Hammer — UCS Correlation
applicability: Miller (1965) correlation for L-type hammer applied horizontally. Apply hammer orientation correction per ISRM for non-horizontal surfaces. Average of top 50% of 20 readings. Alternative correlation: UCS = 6.9 × 10^(0.0087×γ×R+0.16) (Deere & Miller).

title: Terzaghi Scanline Correction for Orientation Bias

λ_true.description: True frequency of the joint set

δ.description: Angle between scanline direction and normal to joint set

applicability: Corrects for geometric bias — scanline parallel to a joint set records zero intersections. As δ approaches 90°, correction becomes infinite (set is invisible to that scanline). Use multiple scanline orientations to capture all sets. Blind zone: joints with δ > 80° effectively unmeasurable on a single scanline.

title: Barton-Bandis Joint Shear Strength (from Field Data)

τ.description: Peak shear strength of the joint

JRC.description: Joint Roughness Coefficient (0–20, measured with profile comb)

JCS.description: Joint wall Compressive Strength (from Schmidt hammer on joint surface)

φr.description: Residual friction angle (from tilt test or Schmidt hammer on saw-cut surface)

applicability: Scale-dependent: JRC and JCS measured on standard 100 mm laboratory sample. For field scale (meters), reduce JRC and JCS using Barton & Bandis (1982) scale corrections. Non-linear strength criterion — curvature controlled by JRC/log(JCS/σn) term.

title: Block Size from Joint Spacing
equation: Vb = S₁ × S₂ × S₃ / (sinγ₁ × sinγ₂ × sinγ₃)

S₁, S₂, S₃.description: Mean spacings of three dominant joint sets

γ₁, γ₂, γ₃.description: Angles between joint sets (all three inter-set angles)

applicability: For three joint sets forming a block. If sets are mutually perpendicular (γ = 90°), sin terms = 1 and Vb = S₁ × S₂ × S₃. Equivalent block side length: lb = Vb^(1/3). Used in GSI estimation and for assessing rippability, blasting, and aggregate source assessment.
